 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. John Harbaugh just told Tom Brady to stay retired, and he did it with a smile that cut deep. The Giants head coach challenged the seven-time Super Bowl champion to prove he could handle the hit, but Harbaugh doesn't think it is possible. "If Tom Brady decided he wanted to come back from retirement, and he actually could, which I doubt for one second he could, no matter what he thinks," Harbaugh told the media, according to Yahoo Sports . He followed that up with a blunt assessment of the physical reality, according to Yahoo Sports : "I don't think he'd be ready the first week as much as you might wanna put him in." This isn't just a playful jab; it is a cold, hard truth about the NFL.
 Brady retired in 2023 after 23 seasons, yet the rumor mill keeps spinning about a return. The legend himself admitted he looked into it, but the league made it clear they were not interested. Speaking while promoting a World Cup advertising campaign, Brady said: "I actually have inquired, and they don't like that idea very much. We explored a lot of different things, and I'm very happily retired. Let me just say that, too." Even his biographer, Lars Anderson, suggests the pull of winning an eighth ring might still be there. Anderson said: "I think he wishes he got number eight. I think he wishes circumstances could have been different and he could have kept playing." But wishing is not the same as playing.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Trenches Are Not a Broadcast Booth
 Harbaugh knows what happens when a 49-year-old body tries to survive the chaos of the offensive line. The Giants are already dealing with a quarterback shuffle, having named J.J. McCarthy as the starter after Jameis Winston struggled against the Saints. McCarthy has played only two games this year, yet he is the one Harbaugh trusts to lead the offense. The idea of bringing in a retired legend as a backup or starter ignores the sheer physical demand of the sport. Brady has 89,214 passing yards and 649 touchdowns, but those stats belong to a different era of his career. The NFL has changed, and the speed of the game has only increased since he hung up his helmet.
 There is also a rulebook barrier that most fans forget. This rule was put in place to stop teams from using equity deals to sign players, and it blocks Brady from even getting on the roster if he wanted to. The Giants need to focus on their current roster, not a fantasy comeback story. Harbaugh is right to call it out. The team is 3-2-1 and heading to Houston on Sunday, Oct. 25, with a real quarterback who knows the playbook.
 Why Harbaugh Is Right About the Giants
 The Giants have bigger problems than a retired quarterback who might want to play. They have a running back room in flux, with Cam Skattebo fighting to keep his job after a rough stretch. He knows he needs to protect the ball after losing one in overtime against Washington. "At the end of the day, I've got to take care of the ball," Skattebo said, according to Yahoo Sports . The focus needs to stay on players who are actually on the field, not ones who are happy in retirement.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Harbaugh's comments serve as a reality check for the entire league. The game is brutal, and it does not care about your past glory. Brady is happy in the broadcast booth, and the Giants are busy trying to win games with the roster they have. The fantasy of a Brady return is over. The reality of the NFL is here, and the Giants are ready for the fight.
